title: Stream diffs as events, with ChangedLines as a collector (step 2.4)
body:
Step 2.4 of the split plan: the streaming event layer, with `ChangedLines` re-implemented as a collector on top of it. Follows the maintainer's answers to the design doc's questions (`docs/diff-model.md`): Q1 (D1), Q2 (D5), Q5 (D9), Q6, Q7, and D11, which 2.3's review deferred to this step.

## What changes

- **Platforms 26 (Q7).** `platforms:` is now macOS, iOS, tvOS, watchOS and visionOS 26, so `Span` and `Array.span` are usable. Linux is unaffected.
- **Event API (D1, `Span` for D5).** `DiffEventParser<Consumer: DiffEventConsumer>` streams `consume(_:)`/`finalize()` like `DiffParser`, and calls the consumer's `mutating` callbacks: `beginFile(_:rawHeader:)`, `beginHunk(_:heading:)`, `line(_:content:)`, `noNewlineAtEndOfFile()`, `binaryPatchLine(_:endsWithCarriageReturn:)`, `endFile()`, `unrecognizedLine(_:endsWithCarriageReturn:)`, and `damage(_:)`. Every callback has a no-op default. Content arrives as a bare `Span<UInt8>`; `[UInt8](copying:)` and `String(decodingLossily:)` copy it out, so consumers never write `unsafe`.
- **Public header types.** `FileHeader`, `HunkHeader`, `FileMode`, `ObjectID`, `DiffPath` and `LineInfo` (kind, old/new numbers, `endsWithCarriageReturn`, `isTruncated`) are public, with memberwise initializers.
- **Line splitter.** Flags a trailing `\r` and truncation at `ParsingOptions.maximumLineLength` (1 MiB by default) per line, identically for any chunking. The marker column counts toward the cap, as `LineInfo.isTruncated` documents.
- **Bounded raw-header buffer.** `rawHeader` is the file's header block verbatim, each line with its `\r` and `\n`; a block past 64 lines or 1 MiB abandons the file with a `headerTooLarge` report instead of growing without limit.
- **`ChangedLines` as a collector.** `ChangedLines.Collector` is a `DiffEventConsumer`; `DiffParser` is now a thin facade over `DiffEventParser<ChangedLines.Collector>` and keeps its API.
- **Damage event (Q6).** `DamageReport` carries the reason, the input line number, the file header (when there is one), and a severity: `info` for a local recovery, `error` for an abandoned file. The library never logs; tools log the event.
- **D9 combined diffs.** `diff --cc`/`diff --combined` files and `@@@` hunks are recognized and skipped with no line events; up to 64 parents are accepted, more abandon the file (`tooManyParents`). An abandoned combined file (too many parents, or an oversized header) drops everything up to the next `diff ` line.
- **D11 epoch timestamps.** A plain-diff `---`/`+++` line whose timestamp is the Unix epoch in any zone (`1970-01-01 01:00:00.000000000 +0100`, `1969-12-31 19:00:00 -0500`) marks the file added or deleted, as git apply's `has_epoch_timestamp` reads it. Apple's diff writes no zone, so its files stay modified, as git sees them too.
- **Docs.** INTERNALS gets an "Events, then collectors" section; the README gets a consumer snippet.

## Accepted divergences from `main` (hostile input only)

None of these occur in git's own output; all three real-world diffs are `cmp`-identical to `main` (below).

- A lone `+++` no longer starts a file (as git apply).
- An unusable `+++` path falls back to the `diff --git` name.
- Hunks under a `diff --git` with no `+++` record under that name.
- `Binary files` outside a header no longer resets the path.
- Abandoned files drop their lines.
- Quoted paths mixing raw invalid bytes with escapes may decode to different U+FFFD runs.
- An epoch-deleted plain-diff file that still adds lines records none (no new path, like `deleted file mode`; git apply refuses it: "deleted file still has contents").

## Tests run

On the PR head, `33a5cc2` (the review fixes), unless noted; the same commands passed on `db28bd5` before them, with 101 tests.

| Command | Inputs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `swift build --build-tests` (from scratch, Swift 6.4) | – | zero warnings |
| `swift test` (network tests on) | full suite; kernel, redis, swift-argument-parser fixtures from the cache | **104 tests in 16 suites pass** (27.0 s); 1 skipped on macOS by design (the GNU-diff epoch case) |
| `xcodebuild test -scheme git-diff-parser -destination platform=macOS` | full suite | **TEST SUCCEEDED**, 104 tests in 16 suites (17.7 s) |
| `swiftlint lint --quiet` | whole tree | prints nothing |
| `docker run swift:6.2` (6.2.4, GNU diffutils 3.10, git 2.43): `swift build --build-tests -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors`, then `swift test` | tree copied into the container, fixtures from the cache | build clean; **104 tests pass** (14.9 s); the GNU-diff case runs here, the Apple-diff case is skipped by design |
| Release harness (`swift build -c release`, chunks into `DiffParser`, prints `path\tlo-hi,...` per sorted path), branch vs `main` at `53e1567` at 4 MiB chunks, then `cmp` | kernel 6.6→6.7 (74 MB, 12,057 files), redis 7.0.0→7.2.0 (7.6 MB, 1,106 files), swift-argument-parser 1.0.0→1.5.0 (0.8 MB, 159 files) | **`cmp` identical** on all three |
| Same harness, branch at chunk sizes 1021, 4093, 65537 and 1048577 bytes, `cmp` against `main`'s 4 MiB output | the same three diffs | **`cmp` identical** on all 12 |
| README consumer snippet, compiled in a package depending on this branch by path (on `db28bd5`) | a hunk declaring 2+2 lines with 1+1 present | builds with no warnings; prints `hunkCutShort line 7 info` (one past the last line, as `DamageReport.lineNumber` documents) |
| `/usr/bin/time -l`, 4 interleaved runs each, release | kernel diff | branch **0.11 s** every run, 22.4 MB peak RSS (17.7 MB footprint); `main` 0.12–0.13 s, 22.6 MB (18.0 MB). At 1 MiB+1 chunks the branch peaks at 14.1 MB: memory follows the chunk size, not the diff |

What the new suites cover (all in the counts above):

- `DiffEventParserTests`: event order and line numbers, pure renames, unrecognized lines, verbatim raw header and heading spans with `\r`, CR/truncation flags at the cap for chunk sizes 1–13, a real `git diff --binary`, no-newline placement, and the whole event stream chunk-invariant on redis and swift-argument-parser.
- `DamageReportTests`: one test per damage reason, with line number, file, severity, and recovery of the next file; 64 parents accepted, 65 abandoned; and the review's regressions: an oversized combined header, misplaced markers between hunks, and a `\ ` line outside any file.
- `CombinedDiffTests`: D9 on real merges built with git: a two-parent conflict resolution with `+++ resolved`, an octopus of 3, `--cc` and `-c`, and the next file after a merge parses.
- `PlainDiffTests`: a real `diff -ruN` against `git apply --summary` and `--numstat -z` (GNU diff, 3 time zones) and, with Apple's diff, numstat only.
- `MalformedInputTests+Headers`: 8 epoch-timestamp regression cases.
- `LineSplittingTests`, `SpanCopyingTests`: the splitter's flags and the copy-out conveniences.

### CI hang, fixed in `4da610c`

**Cause:** swift-testing prints every test argument in full, so `headerTooLarge`'s padding reached the log as a 600 KB and a 1 MB line. GitHub's runner stalls on a line that long and stops draining the step's stdout. Once the pipe is full, every test thread blocks writing its next event, so even trivial tests never finish. A diagnostic watchdog that tried to dump stacks blocked the same way and never printed. Every CI log of the branch ends just before those lines; the longest line logged is 1,338 bytes. **Fix:** the test takes an `OversizedHeader` case and builds the padding itself, and AGENTS.md now says to keep test arguments short. Only a test changed, no parsing code, so the `cmp` and kernel gate above still holds as measured.

| Command | Inputs | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Temporary CI probe job (run 40244854858, since reverted), ubuntu-latest and macos-26 | `printf` one 64 KiB line, then one 1 MiB line, each step limited to 2 min | 64 KiB: printed in 7 s; **1 MiB: never finished, cancelled at its limit on both runners**. This is the hang, reproduced without the suite. |
| Same run, with the fix | full suite on both required jobs | **`tests-and-lint` and `linux-tests` green**: tests in 44 s on macOS, 28 s on Linux (it used to hang until the 30 min timeout) |
| `swift test` output, before vs after the fix (Swift 6.4, network tests on) | full suite | 2.29 MB with 3 lines over 4 KiB (longest 1,048,646 bytes) → **44 KB, longest line 1,283**; 104 tests pass (22.0 s) |
| `xcodebuild test -scheme git-diff-parser -destination platform=macOS` | full suite | **TEST SUCCEEDED**, 104 tests (18.1 s) |
| `swift build --build-tests -Xswiftc -warnings-as-errors`; `swiftlint lint --quiet` | whole tree | zero warnings; prints nothing |
| `docker run --cpuset-cpus=0-2 swift:6.2` (6.2.4, aarch64, git 2.43, nproc 3), output piped | full suite, warnings as errors | **104 tests pass** (13.2 s), longest line 1,281 |

Ruled out on the way: a starved thread pool. A `--cpuset-cpus=0` container still reports 6 online CPUs, but Linux's dispatch pool grows past blocked threads anyway: 24 blocking 1 s tasks finish in 7 s on 1 CPU. Peak RSS of the whole suite is 268 MB.

## Review

Codex (`codex review --base main`, model `gpt-6.1-sol`) on `db28bd5`: **2 findings, both fixed** in `33a5cc2`, each with a regression test that failed before the fix.

1. **[P2] Preserve combined-file skipping after an oversized header** (`DiffEventParser+Headers.swift`). Real: a combined file whose header outgrew its bounds became `.abandoned`, which counts hunks as `@@` ones; its `@@@` hunk didn't parse, so the hunk never opened, and a `--`/`++`-column pair inside it (`--- a/fake`, `+++ b/fake`) began a phantom plain file. **Fixed**: such a file now skips to the next `diff ` line, as one with too many parents already did. Test: `DamageReportTests.combinedHeaderTooLarge`.
2. **[P2] Report misplaced no-newline markers outside hunks** (`DiffEventParser.swift`). Real: a hunk closes at its last line, so a duplicate marker, or one before the first hunk, was handled outside it and forwarded as an unrecognized line with no report, though `misplacedNoNewlineMarker` documents report-and-drop. **Fixed**, with one deliberate limit: within a file, a `\ ` line (git apply's own test) that follows no hunk line is reported and dropped; outside any file it stays an unrecognized line, since it is text there (a format-patch commit message), and dropping it would contradict the parser's promise to pass such text on. Tests: `misplacedNoNewlineMarkerOutsideHunk` (2 cases) and `backslashLineOutsideFile`.

The hang fix: `codex review --base 022ddee` on `4da610c` alone (model `gpt-6.1-sol`): **no findings**. It reran `DamageReportTests` (15 pass) and SwiftLint (clean).
